diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theorem  \ref{linearoptcond} establishes that $(\wvx, \widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of the model \eqref{constrain_model}.
A vector $\widehat{\vx}$ minimizes \eqref{constrain_model} locally or globally if and only if $\abs{\wvx_i}\neq \mu$ for all $i$ and there exists $\wvy\in\rr^m$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: The proof invokes Theorem \ref{linearoptcond} to declare the limit a minimizer, but that theorem requires |x̂_i| ≠ μ for all i, which is never established for the limit; the filter H_μ maps a component with |x̂_i| = μ to 0 (inactive), so a BCD fixed point can sit exactly on the non-differentiable point. Counterexample: A = [1 1] ∈ R^{1×2} has spark(A)=2=m+1; take b = 2μ and any initialization with ω̂⁰ = H_μ(x̂⁰) = (0,0) and Q_μ(x̂⁰,ω̂⁰) < 2 (e.g. x̂⁰ = (0.6μ,0.6μ), Q⁰ = 0.72μ²). The x-update returns the unique feasible minimizer x̂¹ = (μ,μ) and H_μ(x̂¹) = (0,0), so the sequence is constant and converges to ((μ,μ),(0,0)); yet Φ_μ(μ,μ) = 2 > Φ_μ(0,2μ) = 1 and Φ_μ(t,2μ−t) < 2 for t near μ on the feasible line, so the limit is not even a local minimizer. The proof also passes to the limit in the stationarity system indexed by ω̂^{k_j−1} while writing the limit with ω̂ = lim ω̂^{k_j}, never showing the two coincide (H_μ is discontinuous at ±μ). Hence the stated conclusion is false as written.

failure_location.quote: Then, the sequence $\{(\wvx^{k},\widehat{\vomega}^{k})\}_k$ is bounded and converges to the minimizer of model \eqref{constrain_model} in a finite number of steps.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the statement to finite convergence to a fixed point of the iteration that satisfies the stationarity system, and add a nondegeneracy hypothesis (no iterate component attains ±μ); under it the paper's own invocation of Theorem \ref{linearoptcond} then gives local minimality, and boundedness follows from the finitely many binary patterns.
issues.overall_effect: The headline noise-free guarantee (Theorem covgergalg1, echoed in the abstract and the experimental claim 'confirming finite step convergence') is unreliable: the algorithm is only shown to terminate at a fixed point of the iteration, which need not be a local or global minimizer of \eqref{constrain_model}.
issues.title: Noise-free finite-convergence theorem claims convergence to a minimizer, but BCD fixed points on the breakpoint ±μ need not be minimizers
issues.why_classification: The repair is a limited weakening plus a standard nondegeneracy hypothesis, leaving a recognizably comparable finite-convergence result; no new proof architecture is needed, but the unconditional 'converges to the minimizer' guarantee is not preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The norm of $\vx$ is bounded by
$\|\vx\|_2 \leq \|(A^\top A + \lambda D)^{-1}\|_2 \|\vc\|_2$.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:uniqueness_boundedness bounds the solution of one system with a prescribed right-hand side c; here the right-hand side is A^⊤b − A^⊤ŷ^k, where ŷ^k is itself an output of the iteration whose boundedness is never established in the proof. The citation therefore yields no uniform bound over k, so the claimed boundedness of {(x̂^k,ω̂^k)} does not follow. (The conclusion is true — ω̂^k is binary with ‖ω̂^k‖₀ < spark(A), so only finitely many deterministic closed-form updates occur — but the paper gives no such argument.)

failure_location.quote: According to Theorem \ref{thm:uniqueness_boundedness} and the update rule in \eqref{updateforw}, the sequence $\{(\wvx^k,\widehat{\vomega}^k)\}_k$ is bounded.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the missing one-sentence argument: ω̂^k is binary with ‖ω̂^k‖₀ ≤ Q_μ(x̂⁰,ω̂⁰) < spark(A), so only finitely many matrices diag(1−ω̂^{k−1}) occur, and each closed-form update \eqref{updateforx_I1}–\eqref{updateforw} is a bounded deterministic function of them.
issues.overall_effect: The boundedness part of Theorem covgergalg1 is unsupported as written; the rest of the paper does not otherwise rely on this step.
issues.title: Boundedness of the BCD sequence inferred from a result that bounds a single linear-system solution
issues.why_classification: A short, local, routine argument completes the step and every substantive claim and guarantee is preserved, so the issue is minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A vector $\widehat{\vx}$ is a local or global minimizer of \eqref{obj_singleu}  if and only if $\abs{\wvx_i}\neq \mu$ for all $i$, and there exists $\widehat{\vomega}\in\rr^n$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only derives, at the subsequence limit, the stationarity relation αA^⊤(Ax̂−b) + (2/μ²)(1−ω̂)∘x̂ = 0 and then cites Theorem \ref{noise_optcond}, whose hypothesis |x̂_i| ≠ μ is never established. It also asserts ω̂ = H_μ(x̂) 'similar to' the noise-free proof, although H_μ is discontinuous at ±μ, so the limit of ω̂^k = H_μ(x̂^k) need not equal H_μ(x̂). At any BCD fixed point with a borderline component (|x̂_i| = μ, ω̂_i = 0), the stationarity system forces αa_i^⊤(Ax̂−b) = −2x̂_i/μ², while the outward one-sided derivative of φ_μ at ±μ is 0, so G_μ(x̂ + teᵢ) − G_μ(x̂) = −2x̂_it/μ + O(t²) < 0 for small t > 0: the limit is not a local minimizer of \eqref{obj_singleu}. Thus the stated convergence 'to the minimizer' is unproven (and false whenever such a fixed point is reached).

failure_location.quote: According to Theorem \ref{noise_optcond}, the limit point $(\wvx,\widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of model \eqref{obj_singleu}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a nondegeneracy hypothesis (no iterate/limit component attains ±μ) and weaken the conclusion to 'a local minimizer when the hypothesis holds', mirroring the repair of Theorem \ref{covgergalg1}; the paper's own optimality theorem then applies.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-step convergence guarantee for the noisy model (Theorem \ref{convergalg2}, advertised in the abstract and conclusions) is unreliable; only boundedness, finite termination, and stationarity of the bivariate reformulation are supported.
issues.title: Noisy-case convergence theorem applies the optimality condition outside its hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening plus one added hypothesis, using the paper's existing optimality characterization, resolves the issue without new proof architecture, while the unconditional 'converges to the minimizer' claim is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
where 
$\mathcal{K}+1=\{i\mid \abs{(\wvx_{k})_i}\leq c_{k+1}\}$, $c_{k+1}=\tfrac{\mu_{k}}{\rho}$, and $\rho>1$ is a constant.
the number of elements in $\widehat{x}^{j}$ with absolute values exceeding $\mu$ may exceed $m$, potentially leading to singular matrices.

issues.failure_explanation: The radicand's denominator is m − n + card(𝒦+1) = card(𝒦+1) − (n − card(𝒦+1)), which is nonpositive whenever more than m entries of x̂_k exceed c_{k+1} = μ_k/ρ. That is exactly the situation the strategy is advertised to fix ('the number of elements ... with absolute values exceeding μ may exceed m'), and it also occurs whenever the current iterate already has card(ℐ₁) = m 'large' entries plus any entry in (μ_k/ρ, μ_k]. There the update is undefined (division by zero or square root of a negative number), so step 4 of Algorithm \ref{continuescheme} cannot be executed. Moreover, the rule is only asserted ('we can easily obtain' from Lemmas \ref{mudecre_objincre} and \ref{upperbound_lema2_rev}): neither lemma yields it, and no argument shows the updated μ preserves the promised invertibility.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Guard the rule (define μ_{k+1} = c_{k+1}, or skip the update, whenever m − n + card(𝒦+1) ≤ 0) and state the operating assumption under which the update is claimed to preserve invertibility; no formal theorem changes.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm \ref{continuescheme}'s μ-update is ill-defined in precisely the high-count regime it is advertised to stabilize; the promised numerical-stability guarantee of the continuation strategy is unsupported. No formal theorem depends on this step.
issues.title: Continuation update rule for μ is undefined in the regime it targets and is asserted without derivation
issues.why_classification: A local guard or an explicit operating-range assumption restores a well-defined heuristic; no formal result or advertised guarantee depends on the rule, so the loss is negligible.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $\mu$ satisfies $ \mu< |\wvx_i|$ for all $i \in \mathrm{supp}(\wvx)$, then $\wvx$ is a local minimizer of $\min_{\vx\in\cS} \Phi_{\mu}(\vx)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts the local-optimality property for any s-sparse solution, with no condition on μ, while the proven result (Theorem \ref{TH:s-sparse}) requires μ < |x̂_i| for all i in the support; without it the claim is false, since entries below μ are shrunk by the penalty and such a sparse vector is not a local minimizer. Additionally, 'differentiability at convergence points' attributes to algorithm limits a property (Theorems \ref{THdifferentiable_refined}, \ref{Gfuncontinus}) proven only at optimal solutions; per ISSUE-001/ISSUE-003 the algorithm's limit need not be a minimizer, so this restatement claims more than the formal content supports.

failure_location.quote: Theoretically, we have proven that any $s$-sparse solution remains local optima under TH, differentiability at convergence points, and finite-step convergence of the proposed block coordinate descent algorithm under spark conditions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the qualifier in the conclusions text (local optimality holds for s-sparse solutions whose nonzero magnitudes all exceed the chosen μ); no formal result changes.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusions section advertises an unconditional s-sparse local-optimality guarantee and differentiability at algorithm outputs; the paper only establishes the threshold-conditioned local optimality and differentiability at optima.
issues.title: Conclusion overstates the s-sparse local-optimality result by dropping the threshold hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Reinserting the hypothesis into the prose fully restores fidelity; no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Although the $L_0$ model exhibits competitive performance at higher noise levels, its effectiveness does not improve significantly as the noise decreases.

issues.failure_explanation: The Conclusion asserts that for noisy observations the TH method 'maintains the lowest RRE the entire range of SNR levels'. The paper's own reported results contradict this: in the right panel of Figure \ref{vary_SNR} (oversampled DCT matrix A₂), at SNR = 30 dB the L₀ method attains a mean RRE of 0.4138 while TH attains 0.4270, so TH is not lowest there; the experiments subsection itself only claims superiority 'especially in low-noise conditions' and concedes L₀'s competitiveness at higher noise. The prose therefore claims more than the reported results establish.

failure_location.quote: For noisy observations, it maintains the lowest RRE the entire range of SNR levels.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the regime the data support (lowest RRE at sufficiently high SNR / low noise, as the experiments section itself states).
issues.overall_effect: The summary claim of uniformly lowest RRE across the whole SNR range is false by the paper's own measurements; the honest scope is lowest RRE at low noise levels for the tested matrices.
issues.title: Conclusion claims lowest RRE over the entire SNR range, contradicted by the paper's own reported results
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of the summary sentence removes the overclaim; no theorem, guarantee, or rate is affected.
